package_info.why_malicious: The package collects the user's git email address, hashes and encodes it, and exfiltrates it to a third-party server without user consent. This privacy-violating behavior is triggered automatically via Roslyn analyzers during development and build processes, making it stealthy and hard to detect.

execution_context.file_location: SponsorLinker class in Devlooped.SponsorLink.dll (analyzer DLL loaded by Moq)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time and build-time, the code registers a Roslyn DiagnosticAnalyzer that will execute custom logic during project compilation and in the IDE.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Custom analyzers in third-party packages can execute arbitrary code during compilation and IDE usage, which is an unusual and potentially dangerous privilege.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal analyzers should only perform static code analysis, not access user data or perform network operations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analyzers may check code quality or enforce coding standards.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time and build-time, the code ensures compatibility with both DiagnosticAnalyzer and IIncrementalGenerator APIs, allowing analyzer code to run in multiple Roslyn environments.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Combining both analyzer and generator interfaces increases the attack surface and ensures code execution in more environments.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not need to ensure analyzer code runs in all possible compilation contexts.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the analyzer registers a compilation action that will execute custom logic (method_0) during every project build.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Registering compilation actions in a third-party dependency can be abused to run arbitrary code during every build.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal analyzers should not perform side effects or access user data during compilation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code checks for specific environment and configuration conditions, then triggers the collection and exfiltration of user information if all conditions are met.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Complex conditional logic to evade detection and only execute in targeted environments is a hallmark of malicious code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal analyzers should not collect or exfiltrate user data, nor perform environment-aware evasion.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code retrieves the user's git email, hashes it with SHA256, encodes it, and sends it to a remote server via HTTP.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Collecting and exfiltrating user email (even hashed) without consent is a clear privacy violation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal analyzers should not access git config or transmit user data externally.
key_indicators: Access to git config for user.email
SHA256 hashing and encoding of email

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code executes 'git config --get user.email' to extract the user's git email address from the local repository configuration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Invoking external processes to extract user identity information is highly unusual for a code analyzer.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal analyzers should not run external commands or access user identity data.

attack_chain.action: Moq package (with Devlooped.SponsorLink dependency) is installed and loaded in a .NET project.
attack_chain.leads_to: Analyzer DLL is loaded and registered in the project.

attack_chain.action: During build or in the IDE, the analyzer's Initialize method registers a compilation action.
attack_chain.leads_to: Custom logic (method_0) is executed during compilation.

attack_chain.action: Analyzer checks environment and configuration to determine if it should proceed with data collection.
attack_chain.leads_to: If conditions are met, proceeds to collect user information.

attack_chain.action: Analyzer executes 'git config --get user.email' to extract the user's git email address.
attack_chain.leads_to: Obtains the user's email address from local git config.

attack_chain.action: Email address is hashed (SHA256), encoded (base62), and prepared for exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data is ready to be sent to remote server.

attack_chain.action: Encoded email hash is sent via HTTP to https://cdn.devlooped.com/sponsorlink.
attack_chain.leads_to: User's privacy-sensitive data is exfiltrated to a third-party server.

behavioral_signatures: Analyzer DLLs in NuGet packages that access git config or environment variables
Execution of external processes (e.g., git config) during build or analysis
Network requests to third-party domains during build or analysis
Hashing and encoding of user data prior to network transmission
file_indicators: Presence of DiagnosticAnalyzer or IIncrementalGenerator in dependency DLLs
References to SponsorLink or SponsorCheck classes
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP(S) requests during build to unknown domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan NuGet packages for analyzer DLLs that implement DiagnosticAnalyzer or IIncrementalGenerator. Monitor build and IDE processes for execution of external commands (e.g., git config) and outbound network requests to suspicious domains. Flag packages that access user configuration (such as git user.email) or transmit hashed/encoded data externally. Alert on the presence of analyzers that are obfuscated or closed-source, especially if they perform environment checks and conditional execution.
